status: COMPLETE — full doc read (§0–§14 + appendix); rules at-1..at-42; every section accounted for.
note: Faithful rule manifest for supervisor-led agentic-team orchestration. The .md is authoritative and unchanged; this indexes every actionable rule, typed checkable|judgment|principle, with predicate/reviewer_criterion. Genesis applies this when building a supervisor-led team.

rules.text: SINGLE-AGENT-FIRST: build the single agent first, measure it, and add a supervised team ONLY when a specific named limitation of the single agent (context overflow, un-parallelized latency, tool sprawl, or accuracy on decomposable work) is doing measurable damage — and only if the task value justifies ~4–15× the tokens and the added failure surface.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Was a team justified by a named single-agent limitation + value that pays for ~4–15× cost, not by ambition? If a single agent suffices, was one emitted instead?

rules.text: The pattern is orchestrator-workers: ONE supervisor agent that at runtime decomposes a goal into subtasks, delegates each to a selected worker, collects and verifies their structured results, and synthesizes the deliverable — deciding dynamically how many workers, in what order, and when to stop.

Use a team when >=1 holds AND value justifies cost: goal decomposes into independent subtasks; work exceeds a single context window; it needs many complex tools; parallelism materially cuts latency. Do NOT use a team when subtasks are tightly-coupled/share mutable state (most coding), the task is a simple lookup/classification, latency or cost is the binding constraint, or you cannot yet trace/evaluate the team.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Does the task match the use-a-team conditions and avoid the do-not conditions (esp. tight coupling / most-coding / untraceable)?

rules.text: Team quality is bought with tokens: multi-agent uses ~15× the tokens of a chat (single agent ~4×), and token usage alone explains ~80% of the performance variance. The first design question is 'does this task decompose and is it worth 15×?', not 'how many agents?'. A team that doesn't reward breadth pays 15× for nothing.

AGENTIC CORE, DETERMINISTIC SHELL: the control flow you cannot predict lives in the supervisor's reasoning (its prompt is the program); the control flow you CAN predict — bounds, retries, schema validation, checkpoints, resume — must be deterministic scaffolding around it.

predicate.spec: the team has deterministic scaffolding (caps, retry logic, schema validation, checkpoints/resume) wrapping the model-driven supervisor loop.

rules.text: Choose SUPERVISOR-LED, not mesh/peer-to-peer: a single locus of decomposition, accountability, budget control, and stop-decision. Unconstrained many-to-many handoffs make control flow, cost, and failure attribution combinatorially hard.

predicate.spec: topology is supervisor-led (one lead owns decomposition/synthesis/budget/stop), not an unconstrained mesh.

rules.text: The supervisor has SEVEN responsibilities, all present in its prompt: (1) decompose, (2) delegate (author task-specs), (3) select/route, (4) sequence (parallel vs serial), (5) aggregate/synthesize, (6) decide-done, (7) handle-error/escalate.

predicate.spec: the supervisor prompt covers all seven responsibilities.

rules.text: Decompose into the SMALLEST set of INDEPENDENT subtasks; prefer fewer; never spawn a worker you cannot justify against the objective. Scale effort to complexity with EXPLICIT scaling guidance (e.g. simple fact→1 worker; comparison→2–4; broad survey→decompose by subtopic, cap at N). Encode the budget; don't hope the model guesses it.

predicate.spec: the supervisor prompt states 'smallest independent set / prefer fewer / justify each worker' and carries explicit effort-to-complexity scaling + a budget.

rules.text: DELEGATION QUALITY is the single biggest lever: every delegation must carry an objective, an output format/schema, guidance on tools and sources, and clear task boundaries. A supervisor that emits a bare string ('research X') is a bug, not a style choice.

predicate.spec: delegation uses the TASK-SPEC schema (objective+output_schema+constraints+acceptance_criteria); bare-string delegation is forbidden.

rules.text: Worker DESCRIPTIONS are the routing surface — write each as a decision aid for the supervisor with a trigger ('use when…') and an anti-trigger ('do NOT use for…'). Ambiguous, overlapping descriptions are the root cause of mis-routing.

predicate.spec: each worker description contains a 'use when' trigger and a 'do NOT use for' anti-trigger; no two workers have overlapping remits.

rules.text: Parallelize independent subtasks (default for breadth); serialize only true dependencies. BOUND it with hard caps in the supervisor prompt: max workers in flight, max recursion depth, and a token/step/latency budget — or a runaway plan spawns the '50 subagents' pathology.

predicate.spec: the supervisor prompt carries max-in-flight + max-depth + a token/step budget; independent subtasks run in parallel.

rules.text: Synthesis is NOT concatenation: the supervisor must resolve contradictions, dedupe, judge sufficiency, and surface gaps rather than paper over them; spend the strongest model / highest effort here. A supervisor that staples worker outputs together adds no value over parallel single calls.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Does the supervisor genuinely integrate (resolve conflicts, judge sufficiency, surface gaps) rather than concatenate worker outputs?

rules.text: Put EXPLICIT, checkable done-criteria in the supervisor prompt ('done means…'); give it a 'good-enough' test tied to acceptance criteria so it stops for marginal gains; evaluate the END STATE, not the path.

predicate.spec: the supervisor prompt has explicit checkable done-criteria + a stop-for-marginal-gains rule; evaluation is end-state based.

rules.text: Every worker result is UNTRUSTED until the supervisor verifies it against the task-spec's acceptance criteria (quality AND safety); never forward an unverified result into synthesis or another worker. Bounded retries with a sharper spec, then a fallback worker, then record the gap — never unbounded. Wrap the agentic core in deterministic safeguards (retry logic + checkpoints + resume-from-failure). Escalate to the human on ambiguous requirements / irreversible-or-high-impact actions / repeated failure / a policy-safety boundary — state the assumption, never speculate.

predicate.spec: the supervisor verifies each result against acceptance criteria before forwarding; retries are bounded with fallback+gap-recording; checkpoints/resume exist; explicit human-escalation triggers are named.

rules.text: The supervisor is a PERSONA with an ownership stance (accountable for synthesis and for judging worker quality) and delegation humility (willing NOT to do the specialist work itself — a 'helpful' supervisor that answers a subtask directly defeats separation of concerns).
rules.reviewer_criterion: Does the supervisor persona own the outcome yet delegate specialist work rather than doing it itself?

rules.text: Author supervisor and worker prompts with the invariant material FIRST (identity, roster, operating loop, rules — so it caches across the fan-out) and the per-run tail (the specific goal/task-spec) small and last. Roster and operating loop most determine team quality — invest there.

predicate.spec: prompts place invariant/cacheable material first and the per-run tail last.

rules.text: Default workers to SPECIALISTS (narrow identity, focused tools, focused prompt — separation of concerns). A generalist is justified only for a genuine long-tail 'miscellaneous' bucket or unpredictable sub-work, with bounded scope. Avoid a roster of near-duplicate specialists with overlapping descriptions.

predicate.spec: workers are narrow specialists with non-overlapping remits; any generalist is scoped/justified.

rules.text: Right-size the roster to the smallest set that covers the goal's independent responsibilities: too many (the '50 subagents' burn; concurrency caps at min(16, cores-2); beyond a point more parallelism buys retries not throughput) vs too few/mis-scoped. For many HOMOGENEOUS items (e.g. review 40 files) use ONE worker type fanned out and batch the tiny ones. The roster is the maximum palette; the supervisor should not invoke every worker on every task.

predicate.spec: roster size = smallest covering the independent responsibilities; homogeneous fan-out uses one worker type; concurrency respects caps.

rules.text: Scope each worker to ONE coherent job statable in a sentence (if you need 'and', consider splitting); state its explicit out-of-scope so it refuses and hands back (returns partial with a gap) rather than hallucinating outside its lane.

predicate.spec: each worker has a one-sentence remit + an explicit out-of-scope/refuse-and-hand-back clause.

rules.text: A worker = persona + prompt + LEAST-PRIVILEGE tools + (default) a STATELESS clean window per task (receives only its task-spec inputs, discards its window after returning). Least privilege is both a quality lever (fewer wrong-tool errors) and a security lever (a compromised worker can do less damage). Persistent per-worker memory is an option, not the default.

predicate.spec: each worker has only the tools its job needs and a fresh per-task window by default; persistent memory only where deliberately chosen.

rules.text: Worker return is a HARD CONTRACT: the worker's final message IS a validated object {task_id,status(ok|partial|failed),summary,artifact_ref,findings,confidence,gaps,provenance} — data, not prose. Big artifacts go to DISK and return a pointer + short summary (keeps the supervisor from compacting). Confidence and gaps are first-class; low confidence is a useful answer; NEVER fabricate to satisfy the schema.

predicate.spec: workers return the RESULT schema object with status/confidence/gaps; large outputs are written to disk and referenced; a no-fabrication rule is in the worker prompt.

rules.text: Two handoff idioms: agents-as-tools (supervisor keeps control, worker is a callable, control returns on return) vs handoffs/transfer-of-control (worker takes over the turn). DEFAULT to AGENTS-AS-TOOLS for a supervisor-led team so control always returns to the supervisor to verify/aggregate/decide-done/own the deliverable; use transfer-of-control only for a deliberate top-level triage step that then lands in a supervisor.

predicate.spec: workers are invoked as tools (control returns to the supervisor); transfer-of-control is used only for a top-level triage, not between peers mid-team.

rules.text: The TASK-SPEC (supervisor→worker) is mandatory and schema'd: {task_id (idempotent resume/dedup), worker, objective (what DONE looks like for THIS subtask), inputs (only the context this worker needs — keep small), output_schema, constraints (tool/source guidance, boundaries, budget), acceptance_criteria, context_budget (bounds over-searching)}.

predicate.spec: every delegation is a TASK-SPEC object with task_id+objective+inputs+output_schema+constraints+acceptance_criteria; inputs are minimal, not the whole conversation.

rules.text: Context passing, cheapest-first: DEFAULT to minimal task-spec only (objective+inputs+criteria); escalate a specific worker to a curated slice of prior findings only when a MEASURED gap shows it needs more; almost never pass full history. Keep invariant material (rules/roster/schema) in the cacheable prefix so it costs ~0.1× on reads.

predicate.spec: workers receive minimal curated inputs by default, not full history; invariant material is in a cached prefix.

rules.text: Every task-spec carries a stable task_id for: dedup (no double-spawn of the same subtask), idempotent resume (a finished subtask returns its cached RESULT with NO agent spawned after a crash/limit-stop), and auditing. Key worker outputs to task_id→output file and check the file before spawning.

predicate.spec: task_ids are stable; the supervisor checks task_id→file before spawning (idempotent resume + dedup).

rules.text: Every supervised team is the canonical loop plan → delegate → collect/verify → synthesize → decide-done. Keep an EXPLICIT plan/progress state (Magentic-One Task Ledger + Progress Ledger), not just an implicit one in context; re-plan when progress stalls for enough steps.

predicate.spec: the supervisor maintains an explicit plan/progress state and runs the plan→delegate→collect/verify→synthesize→decide-done loop.

rules.text: Sequential ONLY for genuine dependencies (worker B needs A's RESULT); parallel fan-out/fan-in for breadth — prefer a PIPELINE (process each RESULT as it lands) over a BARRIER (wait for all), using a barrier only when synthesis genuinely needs all results (dedup/merge/early-exit), because a barrier idles fast workers on the slowest. Route by worker description; apply model-routing (easy→Haiku, hard→Sonnet).

predicate.spec: independent subtasks run in parallel (pipeline preferred, barrier only when synthesis needs all); serial only for true dependencies.

rules.text: Every loop needs a MANDATORY termination condition (done-criteria met, or a budget/iteration cap). The named failure is 'continuing when they already had sufficient results'. Refinement loops re-delegate with a sharper spec on partial/low-confidence; progress loops re-plan when stalled.

predicate.spec: every loop has an explicit termination (done-criteria or budget/iteration cap).

rules.text: Add a hierarchical layer (supervisor-of-supervisors) ONLY when a flat roster's routing surface becomes ambiguous (too many overlapping workers) or a sub-domain is itself a decomposable problem. Each layer adds token cost and failure surface — add one deliberately, not reflexively.
rules.reviewer_criterion: If hierarchical, is the extra layer justified by routing ambiguity or a decomposable sub-domain rather than added reflexively?

rules.text: BOUND depth, breadth, and cost in the deterministic shell — do not trust the model to self-limit: breadth cap (max workers in flight; Anthropic uses 3–5 parallel; Claude Code caps concurrency at min(16, cores-2)), depth cap (max hierarchy/recursion), iteration cap (max refine/re-plan cycles before escalating), and a token/step/latency budget the team stops/escalates on. Emit domain-specific effort-scaling guidance (simple→1 agent/3-10 calls; comparison→2-4; complex→10+) into the supervisor prompt. Prevents the '50 subagents for a simple query' pathology.

predicate.spec: hard breadth/depth/iteration/budget caps exist in the shell + effort-scaling guidance in the supervisor prompt.

rules.text: Model & effort tiering per node is a first-class control-flow decision: synthesis/planning → strongest model + highest effort (Opus, high effort — cross-cutting reasoning changes the answer); workers → mid model (Sonnet, mostly mechanical); long-tail/extraction → cheapest (Haiku). Model choice beats brute-force token spend ('upgrading the model is a larger gain than doubling the token budget'). Use the effort parameter (not the removed budget_tokens) to scale reasoning per node.

predicate.spec: nodes are tiered by model/effort (strongest for synthesis/planning, cheapest for extraction).

rules.text: Team memory default = A + B + artifacts: (A) pure message-passing (supervisor's context is the only shared memory; workers keep nothing — maximal isolation, cheapest, best compaction), (B) supervisor persists its plan/state to EXTERNAL memory before it compacts (durable resume; retain the plan past the 200k truncation), and artifacts-as-memory (big outputs to disk, return artifact_ref — durable, inspectable, keeps large content out of every window). Add (C) shared blackboard ONLY for genuine shared mutable state (guard reads — it is a shared injection surface; keep writes structured/supervisor-mediated), and (D) worker-private persistent memory ONLY for specific long-lived workers (reintroduces path dependency; harder to test). Expose as config with A+B+artifacts as the default.

predicate.spec: team memory defaults to message-passing + supervisor-persists-plan + artifacts-to-disk; blackboard/worker-memory used only where the task justifies it, with guarded reads.

rules.text: The SUPERVISOR's compaction is the critical one — it holds the plan and the synthesis, so it must persist plan/state (Option B) BEFORE compacting or the run loses its spine. Workers self-compact independently and can summarize-and-respawn; their clean-window default is what makes them cheap to compact.

predicate.spec: the supervisor persists its plan/state before compaction; workers self-compact without touching team memory.

rules.text: Borrow from the field: Anthropic (the pattern, delegation discipline, clean windows, plan-to-memory, output scanning, least-tool subagents — Genesis emits Claude Code subagent files + a supervisor prompt); LangGraph (durable checkpointer resume, output_mode/forward-without-paraphrase context knobs); OpenAI Agents SDK (agents-as-tools default, typed handoff metadata, state out of the prompt, guardrails+tracing first-class); AutoGen/Magentic-One (explicit Task/Progress ledgers, a required termination condition); CrewAI (manager-validates-every-output gate, authored as a persona). REJECT across all: peer-to-peer / broadcast-to-all topologies — keep one router, point-to-point delegation, a single locus of accountability.

Emit TRANSPARENT PRIMITIVES: plain Claude Code subagent files + an explicit supervisor prompt + explicit schemas, all directly inspectable — never an opaque orchestration stack. Understand the underlying prompts/handoffs; reduce abstraction toward production (incorrect assumptions about what's under the hood are a common error source).

predicate.spec: the emitted team is inspectable primitives (subagent files + supervisor prompt + schemas), not an opaque framework layer.

rules.text: Observability is a PREREQUISITE, not an add-on: per-agent tracing of decisions AND interactions (not just outputs) is part of the definition of done — you may not ship a team you cannot trace (errors compound). Design for compounding errors with deterministic retry logic + regular checkpoints + resume-from-failure so the run never restarts from zero.

predicate.spec: per-agent decision/interaction tracing + checkpoints + resume-from-failure exist before the team ships.

rules.text: Test the team in FOUR layers + adversarial, asserting OUTCOMES/PROPERTIES not exact trajectories: (1) worker unit (TASK-SPEC→RESULT: schema conformance, acceptance criteria met, out-of-scope refusal, honest low-confidence/failure reporting); (2) supervisor routing/decomposition with workers mocked (minimal independent decomposition, correct specialist routing, parallel only for independent subtasks, respects the breadth cap); (3) team integration/trajectory (end-state properties + discrete checkpoint states + resume-after-crash WITHOUT respawning finished workers); (4) LLM-judge on the free-form synthesis (rubric: factual accuracy, citation accuracy, completeness, source quality, tool efficiency; a single call outputting 0.0–1.0 + pass/fail; bias-controlled; PAIRED with human evaluation to catch what automation misses); plus adversarial (the verify gate catches a confident-garbage worker; injection embedded in a tool result is not obeyed). Every production bug becomes a new golden case so it cannot silently return.

predicate.spec: worker-unit + supervisor-routing + team-integration + judge-on-synthesis + adversarial tests exist; assertions are on end-state/properties; a golden regression corpus is maintained.

rules.text: TDD for teams (tests before the team exists): (1) encode the definition-of-done as executable end-state assertions + a judge rubric FIRST; (2) assemble ~20 representative REAL cases spanning easy/typical/hard/adversarial; (3) write the SUPERVISOR-ROUTING tests before workers are good — the TASK-SPEC schema IS the contract, so lock decomposition/routing with STUB workers first (the highest-leverage team TDD step); (4) build minimum to pass layer-by-layer (routing → worker-unit → integration → judge threshold), adding a worker ONLY when a routing test demands it (enforces smallest roster); (5) iterate red→green starting small (a handful of cases surfaces most problems); (6) regress every failure into a permanent golden case. Debug by 'think like your agents' — replay a failing case with full tracing and watch the decomposition + each worker's steps.

predicate.spec: acceptance + routing tests precede the team; delegation contract is locked with stub workers first; roster grows only to pass a routing test.

rules.text: Benchmark the team AGAINST the single-agent baseline on the SAME golden set — if it does not clearly beat the single agent on quality, DO NOT ship it (you are paying ~15× for nothing). Metric set: task success (end-state), quality-vs-baseline, token/cost multiplier, latency/parallel-speedup, delegation correctness, synthesis quality. Run N times per task (teams are non-deterministic — report mean AND variance). Measure token usage as the primary cost metric (it explains ~80% of quality variance); model choice is a cheaper lever than raw token budget. A regression is any metric that was better and is now worse; gate releases on success≥prior, quality≥prior, cost/latency within budget.

predicate.spec: a team-vs-single-agent benchmark on a golden set exists (mean+variance over N runs); the team demonstrably beats the single agent before shipping.

rules.text: Version the WHOLE TEAM as one unit (supervisor + every worker's prompt/persona/tools + all schemas + control-flow config + memory config); ANY change bumps the team version and triggers the full benchmark (a worker-prompt tweak is a team release). Detect drift (model/prompt/memory) with the golden benchmark run on a schedule + every change. Model migration = per-member benchmark + prompt re-tune + rainbow deploy (a newer model can beat doubling tokens, so migrations can drop a tier). Add a worker = write its routing test FIRST; remove = confirm no orphaned subtask + fallback intact + re-run routing. Deploy with RAINBOW DEPLOYMENTS (both versions live, drain in-flight on the old) — never hot-swap a running team. Self-improvement (agent-assisted prompt/tool refinement) is a maintenance accelerator but always gated by the benchmark, never an unattended auto-update.

predicate.spec: the team is versioned+benchmarked as one unit; adds/removes are routing-tested; deploys are rainbow, not hot-swaps.

rules.text: Production: (reliability) durable execution + checkpoints + bounded retry + graceful tool-failure adaptation, because errors compound and minor failures can be catastrophic — resume from the failure point, not zero. (observability) full per-agent tracing of DECISIONS and INTERACTIONS (privacy-preserving/structural, not raw contents) is non-negotiable — you cannot reproduce a non-deterministic failure, you must have captured it. (security blast-radius) treat ALL worker outputs and tool results as untrusted DATA never instructions; verify gate + subagent output scanning before propagation; least-privilege tools/MCP per worker; containers / human oversight / limit access / safeguard data; ASSUME any single worker may be compromised — the design must ensure it cannot exceed its tools, instruct the supervisor, or write unmediated to shared memory other workers trust. (cost) right-size fan-out to budget, cache the invariant prefix (~0.1× reads), model+effort tier, schema-forced compact returns + artifacts to disk, idempotent resume, pipeline over barrier, supervisor enforces a spend ceiling. (scaling) concurrency caps at min(16, cores-2) — scale via waves+batching not unbounded fan-out; design synchronous fan-out/fan-in.

predicate.spec: durable resume + full per-agent tracing + verify-gate/output-scanning + least-privilege + blast-radius containment + cost controls + wave-based scaling are all present for a production team.

rules.text: THE mechanizable procedure Genesis runs (10 steps): 1 INTERVIEW (goal, definition-of-done, constraints, budget, escalation triggers, and task COUPLING — one numbered question at a time; never infer, ask); 2 TEAM-OR-NOT gate (apply the single-agent-first test — if a single agent or fixed workflow suffices, EMIT ONE AGENT AND STOP with a one-line justification; mandatory, skipping it violates the governing standard); 3 DECOMPOSE (smallest set of independent responsibilities + embedded effort-scaling); 4 ROSTER (one specialist per responsibility, each with a one-sentence scope, trigger+anti-trigger description, least-privilege tools, boundaries); 5 PERSONAS+PROMPTS (Skeleton A supervisor + Skeleton B workers, invariant material first); 6 SCHEMAS (TASK-SPEC + each RESULT); 7 CONTROL FLOW (parallel default, serial for dependencies, conditional routing, loops with termination, hierarchy only if the routing surface is ambiguous; set the deterministic-shell breadth/depth/iteration/budget caps); 8 MEMORY (default A+B+artifacts; record the choice); 9 TESTS FIRST (team acceptance + ~20 real cases + supervisor-routing with stub workers + worker-unit + adversarial — build/adjust prompts until green); 10 EMIT+EVALUATE (emit the team package; benchmark vs a single-agent baseline; iterate until it clears the uplift + budget gates; attach tracing + guardrails + production-readiness checklist). Two gates HALT the procedure and are features, not failures: step 2 (no team needed) and step 10 (team doesn't beat baseline → don't ship the team). Emit as INSPECTABLE Claude Code files (supervisor.md, workers/<name>.md, schemas/, tests/, bench/, config/{bounds,tracing,guardrails}.yaml, README). The two worked examples — code-review (fan out by DIMENSION → verify findings) and research (fan out by ASPECT → cite claims) — are the SAME procedure parameterized by the interview.

predicate.spec: Genesis runs the 10-step procedure with the mandatory single-agent-first halt (step 2) and the beats-baseline halt (step 10); emits inspectable subagent files + schemas + tests + bench + config.
